decision: Do not promote STATUS ownership from HookedUpdate return or Resident entry gates alone. Prefer a post-publication drain of the pre-existing OS-thread set using conservative complete native stack unwinding, with the conditional no-engine-fiber-yield closure below. Every unknown stack or unresolved older writer keeps bootstrap unavailable.

threadConclusions.motionPool: Six OS worker slots; motion can reach BDX script execution per earlier verified worker evidence. Native job dispatchers join their own batches normally.
threadConclusions.resourceWorker: Separate worker continues independently of update return. No specific STATUS-writing resource callback was identified here. Its mere existence does not prove it writes STATUS; lack of a join prevents treating App return as global quiescence.
threadConclusions.schedulerFibers: Real cooperative engine fibers exist. The examined five-writer normal call closure does not invoke their switch paths; caller code outside a writer can yield safely with respect to this narrowly scoped writer-frame test.
threadConclusions.otherThreads: This report does not enumerate every retail/library/mod thread or prove all possible STATUS writers. A drain must inspect all pre-existing process threads, not only six known motion workers.

normalClosure: 25 native functions, including direct calls and tail jumps. Init EncodeNullable is specialized to its five proven null arguments. Remaining external operations are bsearch with fixed leaf comparator, CRT/Win32 synchronization, and two CFG dispatches whose pointers are initialized to condition-variable APIs.
caveats: No root STATUS function tail-jumps out of its own frame; a descendant call therefore leaves a root return address for a complete unwind under valid unwind metadata.

Normal external API behavior does not call the engine's fiber switch. Imported function identity, dynamic condition-variable pointer identity, relevant native bytes, and fixed comparator must remain intact at runtime.

Arbitrary exception handlers, invalid-parameter handlers, corrupted parameters, externally replaced functions and suspended/resumed foreign contexts are outside the normal closure proof; the stack audit must not declare these safe by inference.
The source entry gate and dynamic trampoline lifetime/unwind behavior require separate implementation and tests. None of the proposed bootstrap algorithm executes in this report.
The known five-entry writer contract remains conditional on the existing STATUS write-family analysis; these captures do not prove no computed or external writer exists.
